key_insight: Commuting diagonal transitions limit SSMs to tracking commutative groups; quaternion channels enable order-sensitive group tracking.
engineering_relevance: HyperSSM preserves linear-time inference and parallel training while enabling compact, interpretable memory for structured sequential tasks.
method: Model sequence updates as a linear representation of the input-sequence monoid.
Characterize group tracking through transition-group quotients and real, complex, and quaternion blocks.
Add quaternion channels in HyperSSM to represent noncommuting transitions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact benchmark group-task solutions using at most five state numbers, including S5 with 32 generators, and generalization to sequences 25× longer than training sequences.
watch_item: The reported successes concern structured group-tracking tasks; broader language-modeling benefits remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
